Q: How to use MySQL's TIME_FORMAT() to convert "H:i:s" time to "h:i p" format A:

Use TIME_FORMAT:

SELECT TIME_FORMAT('14:30:00', '%h:%i %p'); /* 02:30 PM */

Change your PHP to something like this:

$finalresult = mysql_query("SELECT Field1, Field2, TIME_FORMAT(DateField, '%h:%i %p') AS TheTime FROM events WHERE clubID IN (" . implode(',', $clubIDs) . ") ORDER BY date ASC, TIME(startTime) ASC");

This involves getting rid of * and specifying each field you want.

Q: How to measure structural similarity between programs written in different languages A:

Do you want to preserve structural similarity, or are you just trying to measure it for curiosity? If the answer is the former, umm, why are you even using Rust? Otherwise, even with your expanded explanation, it's a little unclear how you define similarity. What makes ? less similar than .is_err() to a return code check in C? In large C code based, I frequently see people writing error-handling macros that conceal a conditional test, optional logging and jump to a cleanup section (bypassing the section that sets the "success" flag in favor of retaining a default or replaced "failure" value), which is basically what ? does for you. What makes a Rust-style for(-each) loop more C-like? Is it still C-like if it's looping over an iterator vs. an index and performing lookup? C literally has no such thing as methods, is it a meaningful change if C uses a "function" like strlen while Rust calls .len() on a &str (or String)?

Those are just a tiny fraction of the programming patterns that Rust supports and C predates (not merely fails to support, the language was designed before the idea themselves existed in any meaningful sense). As a poor analogy, it's like you're asking how similar a particular steam engine design is to an specific electric motor (both steam engines and electric motors can do roughly the same things, it just might be more of a pain to use one or the other for a specific task). If you squint, you can make out similarities, and someone could design their electric motor to work like more like a particular steam engine out of sheer cussedness (let's use the electricity to heat water!), but you can't score the similarity in a useful way.

Q: Next.js: "Cannot find module or type declarations for side-effect import of './globals.css'" ts(2882) A:

There appears to be compatibility issue with Next.js and Typescript v6. Run npm install typescript@5.9 then run through the steps in Guilherme's answer to ensure the app is using the workspace version of typescript.

Q: MySQL get mixed result from 2 queries on same table with different order A:

plan

  • use variable, and order by to rank popularity
  • use variable, and order by to rank recent
  • union all
  • re order by rnk, cat
  • group by id to restrict to first id

input [sample]

+----+---------+--------+--------+--------+------------+----------+--------------------------+--------+--------+--------------+
| id | id_user | title  |  path  |  ext   | image_type | link_url |      creation_date       |  size  |  type  | number_share |
+----+---------+--------+--------+--------+------------+----------+--------------------------+--------+--------+--------------+
|  1 |      22 | (null) | (null) | (null) | (null)     | (null)   | August, 09 2015 10:54:57 | (null) | (null) |            0 |
|  2 |      33 | (null) | (null) | (null) | (null)     | (null)   | August, 09 2015 07:54:57 | (null) | (null) |            0 |
|  3 |      44 | (null) | (null) | (null) | (null)     | (null)   | August, 09 2015 08:54:57 | (null) | (null) |            0 |
+----+---------+--------+--------+--------+------------+----------+--------------------------+--------+--------+--------------+

+------+---------+
| id_b | id_user |
+------+---------+
|    3 |       8 |
|    3 |       9 |
|    3 |      21 |
|    3 |      22 |
|    1 |      55 |
|    3 |      55 |
|    1 |      66 |
|    1 |      77 |
+------+---------+

query

set @rnk_pop := 0;
set @rnk_rec := 0;

-- popularity ranking
select cat, id, rnk
from
(
select cat, id, rnk
from
(
  select cat, id, occurs, @rnk_pop := @rnk_pop + 1 as rnk
  from
  (
    select 'popularity' as cat, A.id, count(B.id_b) as occurs
    from A
    left join B
    on B.id_b = A.id
    group by A.id
    order by occurs desc
  ) q1
) pop_sort
union all
-- recent ranking
select cat, id, rnk
from
(
  select 'recent' as cat, id, @rnk_rec := @rnk_rec + 1 as rnk
  from A
  order by creation_date desc
) rec_sort
order by rnk, cat
) all_q
group by id
order by rnk, cat
;

output

+------------+----+-----+
|    cat     | id | rnk |
+------------+----+-----+
| popularity |  3 |   1 |
| recent     |  1 |   1 |
| popularity |  2 |   3 |
+------------+----+-----+
